market_context: United States; Medjool and other commonly eaten dried dates
title: Dates: sugar, fiber and calories

seo.title: Dates: how much sugar, fiber and how many calories?
seo.meta_description: Dates concentrate sugar because they contain little water, but they also provide fiber and potassium. See values per 100 g, per date and per serving.
seo.search_intent: Learn how much sugar, fiber and calories dates contain and how to interpret those numbers in a realistic serving.

excerpt: Dates are dried fruit, so they concentrate both energy and sugar. Medjool dates provide about 277 calories, 66–67 g of sugars and 6.7 g of fiber per 100 g. Two large dates, roughly 48 g, contain about 133 calories, 32 g of sugars and 3.2 g of fiber. They offer more than sweetness alone, but they are not a low-sugar fruit.
content_html:
A date can taste almost like candy, and there is a reason: with much less water than fresh fruit, its naturally occurring sugars are concentrated into a small bite. Yet a whole date still carries fiber, potassium, and the physical structure of fruit, so calling it “just sugar” misses part of the picture.

The easiest way to understand dates is to use two scales: 100 g for comparison and one or two actual dates for a serving.

What 100 grams of Medjool dates contains

Values vary by variety. USDA reference data for Medjool dates put 100 g at about 277 calories, 75 g of carbohydrate, 66–67 g of sugars, and 6.7 g of fiber. That amount also provides roughly 696 mg of potassium.

Medjool datesApproximate amount
Energy277 kcal/100 g
Sugars66–67 g/100 g
Fiber6.7 g/100 g
Potassium696 mg/100 g

The concentration makes sense when you notice that 100 g of dates contains only about 21 g of water. A fresh apple is roughly 85% water, so drying radically changes how much carbohydrate fits into each bite.

Two Medjools are already a meaningful serving

One large Medjool weighs about 24 g. Two dates, about 48 g, provide roughly 133 calories, 32 g of sugars, and 3.2 g of fiber. One date is about 66 calories, 16 g of sugars, and 1.6 g of fiber.

That is why two dates do not behave like two grapes. It also explains why dates can be useful as compact food before physical activity—and why eating them straight from a large bag can add up quickly.

Is the sugar in dates “natural”?

Yes. In an intact date, the sugars are intrinsic to the fruit, mainly glucose and fructose. Plain dates do not need added sugar to taste sweet, although flavored or coated date products can contain additional sweeteners, so the ingredient list still matters.

“No added sugar” does not mean “low sugar.” Two Medjools contain around 32 g of the fruit's own sugars. The difference from candy is not that those sugar molecules disappear; it is that they arrive with fiber, minerals, and intact plant tissue.

Fiber matters, but it does not erase portion size

At 6.7 g of fiber per 100 g, Medjool dates provide much more fiber than table sugar, which has 0 g. Two dates contribute about 3.2 g—useful, but not enormous compared with what beans, vegetables, and whole grains can contribute across a day.

The need to chew and the fruit matrix make a whole date different from a syrup. Energy density still remains: six large Medjools can exceed 390 calories. Portion size does not stop mattering because the food contains fiber.

A practical way to use their sweetness

Dates work especially well when a small amount sweetens a less-sweet food: chop one into plain yogurt or oatmeal, or pair one or two with nuts. You get the flavor without needing the date to dominate the whole serving.

The useful conclusion is neither “dates have too much sugar” nor “date sugar does not count.” They are nutritious but concentrated dried fruit, and one or two pieces tell you far more about a normal snack than the 100-g number alone.

faq.question: How much sugar is in two Medjool dates?
faq.answer: Two large Medjools weighing about 24 g each contain roughly 32 g of sugars in total.

faq.question: How many calories are in one Medjool date?
faq.answer: A large 24-g Medjool is about 66 calories; two are roughly 133 calories.

faq.question: Do dates have fiber?
faq.answer: Yes. Medjools provide about 6.7 g of fiber per 100 g, or roughly 1.6 g in one 24-g date.
